decisions.statement: Each leading word of the command line steps one level down the command tree.
A word reaches a level only where that level states that word as its name.
A word other than the name of the level it reaches ends the walk.
A level is reached only among the parts the level above it states.
The parts the topmost level states are handed in.
A part is handed back as the levels that part names, or as none.
A level's name, its slug, its page type, its path and its parts come together.
A word that could be no part of a slug ends the walk before that word.
The deepest level the words reach is the level reached.
The levels the walk stepped through to reach a level are carried with it.
Those levels are carried widest first.
The level reached is not among the levels carried with it.
A part naming no level is stepped over rather than ending the descent.
How many words the walk took is carried with the level reached.
The call as it was written is those words with the spaces they were written with.
A level whose own name has a hyphen is reached in one word carrying that hyphen.
The page type a level is under is carried with that level.
A descent starting from no part reaches nothing.
A name more than one level under one level states is carried out whole.
How deep the walk goes is bounded by the words the line offers.
The words reaching a level are each name above that level, ending with its own.
That name is taken off the end of the slug, and what is left names the level above.
A level stating no name is reached by what is left of its slug as one word.
A level whose name is no ending of its slug is reached the same way.
A naming is built over the levels handed in rather than over any list here.
Nothing here loads a page.
Nothing here reads the index.
Nothing here joins words into a slug.
Nothing here decides what the level reached means.
A word naming more than one part ends the walk and steps into none of them.

definition: the level of the command tree a line's words reach, and the words reaching a level
